pattern.crimePattern: merchant smuggling ivory in cement sacks kills the ranger who found it and refused a bribe, and leaves him at a lion kill
pattern.notes: Fictional merchant, conservancy, checkpoint and research project. Lemayian is written as a hero. Ivory concealment is named only as "inside cement sacks"; no routes, buyers or methods beyond that.

ob.text: Conservancy rangers report a colleague, Corporal Lemayian Kantai (35), found dead at 07:00 beside a zebra carcass in the reserve, with lions nearby. Recorded as killed by lions while on night patrol.

people.name: Corporal Lemayian Kantai
people.bio: Alone at the checkpoint on Wednesday night because his partner was off sick. Never took a shilling.

facts.text: Corporal Lemayian Kantai was found dead at 07:00 beside a zebra carcass in the reserve, lions nearby. Recorded as killed by lions on night patrol.
Two head wounds. His rifle and radio are still on him.
At the kill: twin rear tyre tracks of a heavy lorry with dual wheels, off the track and back. No lodge vehicle is that heavy.
His patrol GPS device was switched off and thrown in the grass 20 m from the body.
Collar data: both collared lionesses were 9 km north-east of the kill site from 21:00 to 03:40. They reached the zebra kill at 04:05.
Dr. Sipitiek: "My lions were nowhere near that zebra until four. And lions don't kill a man and walk away from a fresh zebra."
Dr. Sipitiek was at the research camp all night; her collar downloads are timestamped every hour.
Checkpoint logbook, Lemayian's last entry: "22:30 — lorry KCE xxx, hardware, J. Ndwiga — INSPECTING —". The line is unfinished.
Patrol-device server: his position every 5 minutes at the checkpoint all evening. Last position 22:41, at the checkpoint. Then off.
Checkpoint hut: cement dust on the floor and a torn scrap of cement sack with a small pale flake caught in it.
Records, Ndwiga's line: checkpoint zone 22:20–23:00; reserve-interior mast 23:40–00:10; Narok 02:30.
Ndwiga's yard watchman's book: lorry out at 20:15 on Wednesday, back in at 02:30 on Thursday.
Ndwiga's lorry has dual rear tyres matching the tracks at the kill.
In the lorry's load: cement sacks with fine pale dust in their seams.
In the cab, on the owner's side: a jack handle, washed.
Daudi and Kimathi give their fingerprints voluntarily.
Fingerprints taken from Josphat Ndwiga in detention.
Ranger radio log: Faith on duty at the north post all night, checking in every hour from 18:00 to 06:00.
Duty roster note: the Cheruto–Kantai roster dispute was settled by the sergeant on Monday.
Ranger post files: the post's January cement order from Ndwiga Hardware was paid in full.
Patrol reports: no snares on the checkpoint road in a year, and no road accident logged there.
Autopsy: two blows with a heavy metal bar.
Autopsy: no lion bites or claw marks made while he was alive; later scavenging by hyena only. No gunshot; no vehicle or trampling injuries.
Autopsy: death between 22:30 and 23:15.
Lab: the pale flake from the hut and the dust in the sack seams are elephant ivory (cross-hatched growth lines under the microscope).
Lab: Lemayian's blood on the jack handle.
Lab: Ndwiga's prints on the jack handle's grip. Neither Daudi's nor Kimathi's.
Ndwiga: "My lorry was in my Narok yard all night. I never drove that road."
Ndwiga admits his lorry passed the checkpoint at about 22:30 with him in the cab.
Ndwiga: "The corporal waved us through. He was alive at the boom when we drove on."
Daudi: "We didn't go out last night."
Daudi: Lemayian found the tusks; the boss offered him money; he said no and reached for his radio. The boss hit him. They put him in the lorry and Daudi drove where he was told.
Daudi: Kimathi was asleep in the cab. Its inside handle is broken; the boy can only get out when the driver opens the door.
Faith: "I was at the north post all night."
Faith: "We fought about the roster. He was the best of us."
Kimathi: "I was asleep in the cab."
Kimathi: "I'm not allowed to touch the third row of sacks. Never."

interrogations.intro: Ndwiga receives you in his yard office under a photograph of himself with the county governor. "My lorry was in my yard all night. I never drove that road."

topics.reply: A ranger writes many things. Ask him what he meant.

interrogations.intro: Daudi sits on the lorry's step and won't look up. "We didn't go out last night."
Faith stands at attention at the post and her voice shakes. "I was at the north post all night."

topics.reply: We fought about the roster. He was the best of us.

interrogations.intro: Kimathi crouches by the yard gate. "I was asleep in the cab. I can't even open the door from inside."

topics.reply: I'm not allowed to touch the third row. Never. Take my fingerprints. Take Daudi's too.

interrogations.intro: Dr. Sipitiek turns her laptop round so you can see the two tracks. "Look at the times."

contradictions.reaction: Ndwiga adjusts his glasses. "...We passed the checkpoint. The corporal waved us through."
"He found the tusks. The boss offered him money. He said no and picked up his radio. The boss hit him. We put him in the lorry. I drove where he told me. I've vomited every hour since."
Ndwiga takes off his glasses and folds them. "Half a million shillings," he says. "Half a million, and he picked up his radio." He asks for his lawyer.

timeOfDeath.note: From the autopsy; the logbook stops at 22:30 and the device at 22:41.

proof.concludes: The lions were 9 km away until 04:05, and there are no lion injuries from before death. No lion killed him: two blows with a metal bar did.
He was killed at the checkpoint while inspecting Ndwiga's lorry: his log stops mid-line at 22:30 and his device last reported from the checkpoint at 22:41.
The lorry's owner was at the checkpoint and then drove into the reserve, not home; his driver describes the blow.
The lorry's dual tyres made the tracks to the kill, and its cement sacks and the hut floor carry elephant ivory.

The jack handle on the owner's side of the cab carries the corporal's blood and Ndwiga's prints. At the checkpoint, Josphat Ndwiga struck Lemayian with the lorry's jack handle and left him at a lion kill, because the corporal found ivory in his cement sacks and refused a bribe.

eliminations.why: The lions arrived at 04:05, there are no lion wounds from life, and a lorry's tracks lead to the body.
His device never left the checkpoint until it went dark.
He was at the checkpoint; the lorry wasn't back in the yard until 02:30.
His device and logbook put him at the checkpoint when he died.
Daudi was there and helped move the body; he will be charged as an accessory. The handle carries Ndwiga's prints, not his.
Kimathi was asleep in the cab, which he can't open from inside.
Faith checked in every hour from the north post.
Dr. Sipitiek was at the research camp; her downloads are timestamped.
The lions were 9 km away, and no lion wounded him in life.
Two bar blows, no vehicle injuries.
Settled on Monday, and Faith was at her post.
No snares on that road in a year.
The post's cement order was paid.
No road accident was ever logged.

reconstruction.text: For a year Ndwiga's lorry carries cement and roofing to the lodges, and, in the third row of sacks, elephant ivory from the borderlands to buyers in Narok.
Wednesday, 22:30. Corporal Lemayian Kantai, alone at the checkpoint, stops the lorry and writes in his log: INSPECTING. In the third sack he finds a tusk.
Ndwiga offers him KSh 500,000. He refuses and reaches for his radio. Ndwiga strikes him twice with the jack handle.

With Daudi's help he loads the corporal into the lorry, drives into the reserve, and leaves him beside a fresh zebra kill. He switches off the patrol device and throws it in the grass. At 02:30 the lorry is back in Narok.
At 04:05 the lionesses reach the zebra. At 07:00 the rangers find their colleague. They attend the reconstruction in full uniform.

clockPlan.note: Records on Ndwiga's line, then a warrant on the lorry. Detain him at the yard; his prints come back in 6 h and the trace and ivory in 12 h, inside the 24 hours.
